boxes.text:
Can popular music predict
U.S. recessions?
Do lyric emotions add value beyond the Treasury yield spread?
Observed music-model loss is higher; robust statistical degradation is not established.
Keefer Wu · Nathan Starkman · Kiran Reddy Bhumireddy
Three data sources; one frozen measurement model
Music study: 1973–2023 · economic history extends earlier
GS10, TB3MS and USREC: yields and recession labels.
Weekly chart identities matched to historical lyrics.
Six emotion scores; trained on Reddit, unvalidated on these lyrics.
Automated-screen eligibility is not recording verification or rights clearance.
Coverage changes the population we evaluate
Median monthly share of chart popularity weight scored
Unverified identities and shifting songs remain even when the coverage gate passes.
Source audit → frozen measurement → paired chronological evaluation
Keep valid weekly appearances and ranks.
Reconcile title, artist and source; retain exclusions.
Six emotion means + continuous spread at month t.
Expanding Probit fits; save probabilities and dates.
The existing model already uses the magnitude of the yield spread
Model A: p_A(t+6) = Φ(β0 + β1 spread_t)
Model B: p_B(t+6) = Φ(β0 + β1 spread_t + γ′E_t)
Joy · sadness · fear · anger · nervousness · optimism
Six preselected emotions; training-only scaling; no PCA or score-driven feature search.
The six-month index starts at the predictor month
Train on the same eligible rows from January 1973; require at least 240 actual observations.
Training target i+6 ≤ t−1  so  training predictor i ≤ t−7.
Example: November 1993 predictor → December 15 issuance → May 1994 target.
Observed loss rises when music is added
70% primary · the same 183 dates · 15 recession months · 3 episodes
B − paired A = +0.029867; neither beats the training-rate reference here.
Average precision is stepwise AP, not trapezoidal precision–recall area
Higher thresholds remove entire recession episodes and change both training and evaluation dates.
Primary sample · conditional on saved predictions and selected calendar
95% circular calendar block-bootstrap intervals for mean Brier B − A
Four limits define what we can claim
A negative result does not identify its cause
15 positive primary months from only 3 recessions; nested samples.
Unverified matches and language; declining coverage; NLP unvalidated on lyrics.
Final vintages, retrospective labels and uncertain source publication times.
Earlier audit: 7,490 shared vectors match; 8,800 songs lack a current-hash rerun.
An auditable comparison, with a qualified negative finding
Observed music-model performance is worse on the selected samples.
Robust statistical degradation is not established.
Contribution: implemented pipeline, paired evaluation and explicit reproduction limits.
Next research priority: validate measurement and historical availability before redesigning models.
Appendix A · all existing uncertainty settings
Circular percentile intervals and approximate HAC references are different approximations
Appendix B · scores and descriptive diagnostics
Compare A/B within each sample; higher-threshold dates are nested
Calibration: 44 evaluated B probabilities in [0.3,0.8), including 1 recession.
Training events per parameter: 46–61 positives / 8 parameters = 5.75–7.625.
Sparse lag-24 cross-product ratio at 80%: 3.3566 from 3 pairs; not a correlation.
Offline derived-result checks do not establish full current-code NLP inference
Verify metrics, calibration, same-date benchmarks and conditional inference offline.
Regenerate the original ten figures without raw lyrics or model downloads.
Requires external raw sources, audit inputs, weights and compatible caches.
Historical validation: 215 tests passed at PR #2 head; numerical code is unchanged in final delivery.
Appendix D · CRISP-DM and justified decisions
Delivery is a reproducible research bundle; no deployment claim
Question, economic baseline, source and coverage audit.
Match, screen, chunk, rank-weight and join by calendar month.
Paired Probit; chronological refits; probability loss and conditional inference.
Report, timed deck, saved outputs and reproducibility limits.
No PCA: six interpretable preselected features. No random split: preserve chronology. No score-driven extra models.
Appendix E · references and TA clarification
Detailed links and source versions are in the final report
Sources: FRED GS10 / TB3MS / USREC; weekly Billboard archive; OSF historical lyrics.
Measurement: pinned SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions; estimator: statsmodels Probit.
Evidence: original predictions/metrics, closeout verification and paired_inference.json.
TA question: continuous spread magnitude is already implemented. Did you intend a change in spread, or a different target?
